artifacts.title: WonderCMS RCE to SSH and log injection root (Sea)
artifacts.starting_access: unauthenticated web access to a WonderCMS bike page on sea.htb
artifacts.outcome: root via command injection in a system-monitor log analyzer
transferable_properties: fuzz themes folders to find CMS version README files
a contact form can deliver an exploit link for the admin to click
crack bcrypt hashes with hashcat mode 3200
use SSH port forwarding to reach internal services
URL-encode RCE payloads in web forms (CTRL+U in Burp)

hypotheses.statement: the WonderCMS version is vulnerable to a public RCE

selected_action.intent: identify the CMS version and locate a public exploit

evidence.summary: found WonderCMS 3.2.0 via /themes/bike/README.md, vulnerable to CVE-2023-41425

observations: CVE-2023-41425 installs a malicious theme module
the admin must click the exploit link

hypotheses.statement: delivering the exploit link via the contact form triggers a reverse shell

selected_action.intent: run the exploit, send the link via the contact form, and catch a reverse shell

evidence.summary: sent the exploit link through /contact.php, the admin clicked it, and a reverse shell returned as www-data

observations: database.js in /var/www/sea/data contains a bcrypt password hash

hypotheses.statement: cracking the hash yields a password reused for SSH

selected_action.intent: crack the bcrypt hash and try it over SSH

evidence.summary: cracked the hash with hashcat mode 3200 and logged in over SSH as amay

observations: an HTTP server runs on internal port 8080

hypotheses.statement: the internal system-monitor web app has a command injection

selected_action.intent: forward port 8080 over SSH and inject a command into the log analyzer

evidence.summary: found a log analyzer form vulnerable to command injection and obtained a root reverse shell
